> **AI-generated review used during development — not a review by a human aviation professional.**

# Cutaway critique, round 1

**Page:** `docs/lab/cutaway.html` (drawings from `docs/assets/svg/cutaway.svg` and `cutaway-simple.svg`, generated by `docs/assets/svg/src/cutaway.mjs`)
**Viewports:** 1440×900 (DPR 2) and 390×844 (DPR 3, touch)
**Reviewer stance:** a principal illustrator who grew up on classic aviation cutaway posters.

Capture note: Playwright `full_page` screenshots caught a re-draw state where the parts were missing and the lines were half drawn. That looks like a capture artifact, because the normal viewport captures are clean, so those files were removed. Someone should still check by hand that a real window resize never re-runs the draw-in.

## Interaction test results

- **Hover (part body):** works. The card appears, the other parts dim to 38 %, and the active leader and tag light up. Good.
- **Hover (label):** works, but the card sits on top of the hovered label and the labels around it. For label 20 the card measures 330×437 px and its bottom edge is at y = 1017, past the 900 px viewport.
- **Card position:** the card often covers the label column (part 05 hides labels 01–09) or the bottom callouts (part 03 hides 12/13). The "never cover the part" rule works. Nothing stops the card covering the active label.
- **Keyboard:** tab order runs 01 → 26 in numeric order with useful aria-labels, which is good. Focus brackets show. Escape hides the card. Enter/Space go to the part page.
  - **Bug:** pressing Tab from 26 moves focus to "Open part page" inside the card. The card then hides after 120 ms and focus drops to `<body>`. Keyboard users lose their place.
- **Click → part page:** clicking part 03 goes to `index.html#/parts?pn=GN-32-R017`. Correct.
- **Phone list:** 26 rows, each at least 48 px tall, as `aria-expanded` disclosures. Opening one drops a ring and number badge onto the sticky drawing. The open row shows the full facts card and the link. There is no horizontal scroll (scrollWidth 390). Works well.
- **Console:** no errors.
- **Copy:** "holds 1 spares" needs a singular form. The lede says "Hover … click" on phones, where the action is a tap on a list row.

## Originality check

- The drawing is built in code from a simple 3-D model (`cutaway.mjs`, 1,029 lines of procedural geometry). It is a coherent generic twin-jet: low wing, two underwing engines, conventional tail, winglets. Nothing looks traced. The line quality is uniform in the way generated geometry is, not in the way a trace is.
- No manufacturer names, type designations, logos or liveries appear in the SVG text or the generator. A grep for Airbus, Boeing, A320, Embraer and livery found nothing; the only "737" hits are coordinates. All part numbers are fictional `GN-` numbers. The title block says "GENERIC NARROWBODY · SCHEMATIC — NOT ENGINEERING DATA".
- One small risk: the title block says **LENGTH 37.6 m**, which is almost exactly the published length of one well-known narrowbody. Change the figures to clearly generic values (for example 36.8 m length, 33.9 m span, 11.9 m height) so nobody reads it as a specific type.

## Scores (1–5)

| Criterion | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Craft** | **2.5** | The projection is consistent because it comes from a real 3-D model: frames, windows and nacelle ellipses all agree, and that matters. But nearly every line has the same weight. The silhouette is 1.35 units (≈1.2 px on screen); interior lines are 0.6 units at 24–40 % opacity (≈0.5 px, close to invisible on a 1× screen). There is no hidden-line priority and no tonal depth. There are anatomy errors: the main wheels and brake (16/17) float behind the engine on the pylon with no gear leg or wheel well. The nose wheel hangs below the fuselage on a hairline with a visible gap. The wing is a flat sheet with no thickness. The fin is a flat plate. The cabin interior is a scribble of seat boxes that reads as noise. |
| **Detail** | **2.5** | Present: frames and stringers, window rows, aft pressure dome, cabin seats, some wing ribs in the cut panel, fan face, part primitives. Missing: floor beams, keel, cargo hold, wing box spars, centre wing box, gear bays, doors, flight-deck furniture, engine core stages, and all system runs (bleed ducts, hydraulic lines, fuel feed, wiring looms). Every part is a box or cylinder glyph, so nothing reads as a pump, valve or computer. |
| **Legibility** | **3.5** | Callouts are clean: numbered mono tags, numeric order clockwise from the nose, dot ends on the parts, and the active-state dimming is good. Against that, the left fan of ten leaders crosses itself and the 15.3 m dimension. Leaders 25/26 drop about 700 px from the top edge across the whole fuselage. Names render at about 12 px and the dimension text at about 9.4 px. The card is rich and well written but too tall (≈440 px) and covers labels. The phone drawing's part glyphs are about 6 px with no numbers until you pick one. The phone list itself is very legible. |
| **Brand fit** | **4.0** | The palette lands: #09131F field, faint teal blueprint grid, titanium ghost lines, glowing teal parts, copper cut edges, a mono title block with a copper tick, and Plex Mono numbers. Points off because callout names are set in Inter, not Plex Mono, and copper is under-used. It appears only as three thin cut outlines, with no hatching or tone. |
| **Would a cutaway-poster fan admire it?** | **2.5** | It reads as a well-designed interactive diagram, not yet a cutaway. A fan looks for the plane's insides (structure, systems, depth, weighted line) and for clever cut planes. Here the skin is outlined, not peeled. There is no section face, no density gradient that pulls the eye to the cut, and the floating gear would be spotted in seconds. |

**Mean: (2.5 + 2.5 + 3.5 + 4.0 + 2.5) / 5 = 3.0**

## Top 8 improvements (priority order)

### 1. Fix the anatomy errors first (gear, pylon, wing thickness)
- **Main gear:** move parts 16 (wheel and tyre) and 17 (carbon brake) off the pylon. Place them at the wing-root trailing edge, about 0.38 of fuselage length behind the wing leading edge at the root and about 2.2 m outboard of the centreline. Add a main gear leg: an oleo cylinder from the wing rear spar down to the axle, with a side brace and torque link. Draw a wheel well in the fuselage belly behind the wing box as a rounded rectangle with door hinge lines. Show both bogies, with the far one at ghost opacity.
- **Nose gear:** connect the nose wheel to a strut that rises into a nose-gear bay under the flight deck. Draw the bay as a box with two door outlines. Add a drag brace. Remove the gap between strut and wheel so the axle sits on the strut's end.
- **Pylon:** draw it as a swept box from the nacelle top to the wing lower surface (four edges plus a fairing curve). Parts 13/14/15 then sit on visible structure.
- **Wing and fin thickness:** extrude the wing to a thickness/chord ratio of about 0.11 at the root and 0.09 at the tip. Draw the near-wing leading-edge and trailing-edge upper and lower lines and close the tip. Give the fin and stabilisers a leading-edge radius line and a closed tip.

### 2. Set up a real line-weight hierarchy and depth cue
Use these weights in viewBox units, at 1600 wide:

| Tier | What | Weight | Opacity | Colour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Outer silhouette, near side only | 2.0 | 0.95 | titanium #C9D4DF |
| T2 | Cut edges | 1.6 | 1.0 | copper #C47F52 |
| T3 | Primary structure: frames at every 4th station, spars, bulkheads, floor beams | 0.9 | 0.55 | titanium |
| T4 | Secondary: stringers, seats, ribs | 0.5 | 0.22 | titanium |
| T5 | Far-side and hidden lines | 0.5 | 0.12 | titanium, dash 3 3 |

- Sort lines by depth: the near surface fully opaque, the far side faded. Opacity can be a linear function of the model's z coordinate.
- Cull seat boxes on the far half of the cabin. They create most of the moiré "scribble".
- Line ends: round caps on T1–T2, butt caps on T3–T5.

### 3. Turn the outline cut into a real cutaway: peeled skin and section faces
- Replace the smooth copper curve with a **jagged torn-skin edge**: a zig-zag polyline with stringer stubs, 3–6 units long, sticking out past the edge at each stringer crossing.
- Fill a thin **section face** along the cut, 4–6 units wide, with 45° copper hatching (0.4 weight, 3-unit spacing, 0.5 opacity). This one move makes it read as a cutaway.
- Add a slight dark radial vignette (#060E17 at the edges) behind the fuselage, plus a soft teal glow (opacity 0.06) inside the cut window. Together they pull the eye into the opening.
- Open a second cut on the near engine nacelle with the same treatment. Show fan blades as 18–22 radial spokes, three compressor stage discs, a combustor ring and a turbine cone.

### 4. Add structure density where the eye lands
Inside the cut windows, at tier T3, draw:
- floor beams and seat tracks;
- a keel beam and the lower-lobe **cargo hold**, with 3–4 container or bag outlines;
- the **centre wing box** (front and rear spar, 4 ribs);
- the near-wing **front and rear spar** plus ribs every ~1.2 m in the cut panel;
- passenger and service door outlines (2 fwd, 2 aft);
- the flight-deck: two seats, glareshield, centre pedestal;
- avionics racks in the electronics bay under the flight deck. Parts 03–06 then sit in racks instead of floating.

Keep the density highest at the cut and let it fall away towards the tail and the far side.

### 5. Draw the system runs and link them to hover
- Add schematic routes as smooth splines at 0.8 weight, teal #22C7B8, opacity 0.25:
  - **bleed air:** engine (15) → pylon → pack bay (02 → 01);
  - **hydraulics:** EDP (13) → PTU (25) → servo controls (18/20/23), with 3 colour-coded lines (teal dash patterns 0, 4-2 and 1-2);
  - **fuel:** tank → boost pump (26) → engine;
  - **electrical:** IDG (14) → TRU (05) → avionics bay.
- On hover or focus, raise the active part's system route to opacity 0.9 with the `cw-glow` filter. Animate `stroke-dashoffset` along the route for about 600 ms; skip the animation under reduced motion.
- This turns isolated glyphs into a story, and it is the most portfolio-worthy upgrade.
- While here, give each part a recognisable silhouette instead of generic primitives:
  - pumps: a cylinder with a flange and two port nubs;
  - valves: a butterfly body with an actuator box;
  - LRUs: a box with a front-panel handle and a connector strip;
  - wheels: tyre torus plus hub plus brake disc stack.

### 6. Re-lay the callouts: shorter leaders, no crossings, Plex Mono names
- Assign labels to the **side nearest each part**. Sort each side by the parts' projected y position so leaders never cross. Example: nose parts 07–12 go bottom-left, cabin parts 01–06 top-left, and 25/26 move to the bottom edge beside 13–15 instead of dropping 700 px from the top.
- Use **elbow leaders**: one segment at 30–45° from the part, then a horizontal run of 24–60 units into the tag. Cap the total length at about 320 units. Add a 3-unit #09131F halo (already present) so leaders stay clean over the structure.
- Set names in **IBM Plex Mono 500**, 13–14 units, letter-spacing 0.02em, so they render at ≥12 px at 1440 and match the brand brief. Keep two-line wraps right-aligned on the left side and left-aligned on the right side, as now.
- Remove or relabel the unexplained diagonal **15.3 m** dimension, which crosses five leaders. Replace it with an overall-length dimension along the belly and a span dimension at the wingtips, both in the empty bottom band.
- Change the title-block numbers to clearly generic values (see the originality note).

### 7. Card behaviour: dock it, keep it out of the way, fix focus
- **Desktop:** stop floating the card over the drawing. Dock it to the empty bottom-left quadrant (the legend area, about 360×420 units, with the legend moved up). Or dock it as a 340 px right rail that slides in, with the drawing shifted 170 px left. Keep a 1.3-weight teal connector from the card edge to the active part so the link stays visible.
- If floating is kept, the placement must skip any spot that covers (a) the active part, (b) the active label and (c) more than two other labels. Clamp the card to the **visible viewport** (`window.innerHeight`) rather than the stage. Today it runs off the bottom at 1440×900.
- **Make it compact:** lay facts out in a 2×2 grid (removals | repair time / spares chips | hours grounded). Cut the vertical padding. Collapse planner flags to one line with a "+2 flags" chip. Target ≤ 300 px tall.
- **Focus bug:** while the card is not pinned, set `tabindex="-1"` on its link so Tab from 26 leaves the SVG cleanly. Or, if keyboard users should be able to reach the link, cancel `hide()` while focus is inside the card (`card.contains(document.activeElement)`).
- Fix the plural: "1 spare" vs "N spares".
- Fit the whole poster above the fold at 1440×900. Cap the stage with `max-height: calc(100vh - 140px)` and centre the SVG with `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"`, or shorten the header (drop the lede to one line on wide screens). Today callouts 12–15, the engine and the gear sit below the fold.

### 8. Phone layout: more drawing, zoned list, tap-friendly
- The simplified drawing is too sparse: an outline only, so it reads like an icon. Keep T1 silhouette, cut edges and the primary T3 structure. Raise part glyph size by about 1.8× and draw small **number dots** (≥9 px mono, teal on #09131F) next to each part, clustered with 4 px offsets in the nose bay.
- Crop the phone drawing tighter so the fuselage fills about 95 % of the width. Rotate the camera about 8° flatter so the plane is longer and less tall in the 220 px sticky frame. Reserve the top-right corner for a 2.5× **zoom inset** of the selected part's zone.
- Give the drawing invisible 44×44 px hit targets per part. Today the tiny glyphs are hard to tap.
- Group the list under zone headers: Flight deck and nose (07–12), Cabin and avionics (01–06), Wing (18–21, 26), Engine and pylon (13–15), Landing gear (16–17), Tail and APU (22–25). Use small Plex Mono uppercase headers with a copper tick. Rows can then drop the part number to a second line in 11 px and stop wrapping long names.
- Use phone-specific lede copy: "Tap a number or a row to see its facts."
- When a row opens, scroll the open row's top to sit just under the sticky figure (`scroll-margin-top: 236px`) so the marker and facts are seen together.

## What already works (keep it)
- The projection, built from a 3-D model, is coherent and believable. Do not hand-redraw it; improve it at the generator level (`cutaway.mjs`).
- The draw-in (2 s, reduced-motion safe), the dim-others focus state, the focus brackets, the numeric tab order and the aria-labels are all good.
- The title block, legend and orientation triad give the "drawing sheet" feel. Keep them, but tighten them.
- The phone disclosure list with the marker on the sticky figure is a sound pattern.
